utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Before our next witness is brought in, I would like to raise two issues with the parties. The first issue about the testimony by Defence witnesses about the character of the accused. Now, I went through the transcripts and I found a statement made by the Prosecutor on the 27th of January, Mr. Terrier, where he said and I quote, "As far as the Prosecution is concerned, there's no doubt as to the character of the witnesses. We are not aiming to prove before this Court that the accused, before the conflict, were horrible human beings who had terrify relations with their Muslim neighbours. I think the contrary is true, and we're not contesting that particular point." In light of this statement, I think it is the character -- the good character of the accused is not an issue in dispute, so, therefore, we should not waste our time hearing witnesses here who testify about the character of the accused. Please, therefore, refrain from asking any questions about their character, because as I say, this is not an issue which is in dispute. The Prosecutor is not disputing the good character of the witnesses. Second point about the possible testimony by witnesses, Defence witnesses, on massacres or alleged massacres or atrocities committed by Muslims. Again, at least we have raised the question of the extent -- on whether what extent this issue was material to our case. In spite of our repeated appeals, the Defence counsel have continued raising issues relating to the massacres committed by Muslims. Now, from now onwards we would like to ask the Defence counsel, if they intend to go into this matter, before they do so to explain the relevance of the testimony on this particular matter to our case, so that we can decide whether or not this evidence is admissible. I think this is a sort of fair compromise to take account of the rights of the Defence while at the same time safeguarding the rights of the accused to an expeditious trial. We will now, if there are no matters to be raised by the parties, we are in a position to move on and, I would like to ask the registrar -- yes, Counsel Susak first and then Counsel Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, we had a discussion on Friday, and the Presiding Judge was Judge May. He requested me to inform him when the gate in the warehouse was filmed. This was done on the 18th of December, 1998. That is my answer that I owe him. I see that there was some confusion in the courtroom, so allow me to say a few words. This is the western gate of which a photograph was taken by SFOR on the 17th of April, and that is the gate on the videotape and on the photograph taken on the 18th of December, 1998. There is another gate shown on another photograph which the Prosecutor has tendered into evidence, and that is on the southern side and facing the road, and many did not realise that there were two gates, and this one on the west is the one shown on the photograph in the video. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have heard your ruling regarding witnesses that may be called as character witnesses. The fact that the Prosecutor agrees that these are persons with a good character can be considered mitigating circumstances. However, we wanted those witnesses to be heard to illustrate a model of behaviour on the part of the accused, which is part of the factual evidence, and this model of behaviour is used to prove whether anyone is guilty of anything, and it is envisaged in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. A certain model of behaviour throughout a person's lifetime shows whether a perpetrator could have been a perpetrator at all at a point in his life, and that is why the Rules of Procedure and Evidence envisaged the proving of this model of behaviour in the Court of the proceedings. So we are using this testimony as factual evidence rather than character evidence, that is, to illustrate a certain model of behaviour, not to testify to the character of the accused but to the model of behaviour applied by the accused throughout his lifetime. Regarding your other rulings, we would like to ask to receive it in writing, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Mr. President, last week when Judge May was the Presiding Judge, I asked a question and asked the Trial Chamber to help me deal to with it. I'm referring to your ruling and its implementation regarding the possibility of the Defence to provide investigators with a contact with witnesses. The place where this interview would be held remained disputed. The Defence organised it in Vitez and the Prosecution, for security reasons, at least that is the reason they give, have proposed Sarajevo. I, therefore, asked a decision to be taken about this, because we have fixed the 20th of February, and we have notified you on time about this. Could you please address this matter because it appears the two parties are unable to come to an agreement. If security is in question, and if the Prosecutor can provide security for the Defence witnesses in Sarajevo, I see no reason why that same kind of security would not protect the investigators when they come to Vitez. So I ask you kindly, and I apologise for taking up your time with this, to help us deal with this matter and come to a solution, a matter which we consider to be important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Pavkovic. We will, of course, issue a written ruling as requested by Counsel Radovic on the question of the tu quoque principle. We will also issue a reflection. Probably it's better for us to issue also a ruling in -- a written ruling on this issue of character witnesses, to see whether the argument made by Counsel Radovic about the model of behaviour of the accused is relevant. As for the question of -- just raised by Counsel Pavkovic, let me ask the Prosecution to see whether they can offer the solution. I would be grateful to the Prosecution if they could also say a few words -- a comment on the other two points, to the issues I raised this morning. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. President. In response to Mr. Pavkovic with regards that question; yes, indeed it was brought up last Thursday. Judge May had requested that a compromise be reached between Mr. Pavkovic and the Prosecution. I'd like to repeat that for our own reasons and for reasons of security, which were particularly underlined by SFOR, it is not possible to go to Hotel Vitez to carry out interviews at Hotel Vitez. However, we may make another proposal to Mr. Pavkovic, which would be to meet in Zagreb. We believe this compromise is acceptable to Mr. Pavkovic and to the witnesses who, in a way, they represent. Then this meeting can take place at the office of the prosecutor in Zagreb with, of course, all parties. The security of all parties, of course, will be assured there. That's the first point. In respect of the second point you underlined, Mr. President, in response to Mr. Radovic, the Prosecution reiterates its declaration in which, yes, indeed, we have not yet indicated that any of the Prosecutors (sic) had, before the war, any type of unfavourable behaviour or criminal behaviour, or that the behaviour of the accused before the war can explain the crimes of which they are accused today. Mr. Radovic made a statement which, if you will, is philosophically stated that the criminal behaviour can be -- always explained by the behaviour of the person since their childhood, and that the biography of an accused -- in one's biography one would always find history of crime. However, we believe that in the particular circumstances, or to the ones that we are to examine -- which we must examine and which the Tribunal will examine that, the explanation of the crime will not necessarily be found in the biography of the accused but rather in the circumstances which will be submitted to this Trial Chamber. So we believe, indeed, that the character witness who have come to talk about the behaviour of the accused before the war will not be relevant to this trial, and we believe that the decision that was made by this Trial Chamber was very much incontestable. Mr. President, would you like for the Prosecution to give its point of view on other aspects as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, on the relevance of the presentation of witnesses dealing with massacres committed by Muslims against the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. President, the Prosecution does not contest that in the circumstances of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time that there were massacres committed against the Croat population, and that since we are not here to contest the evidence which will be submitted to the Tribunal in this vein. However, it may be useful for this Tribunal to know the context in Bosnia-Herzegovina at this time, in the early months of 1993, in the last months of 1992, however, we do not believe that we should necessarily use too much time in this area. We believe already that we have heard witnesses by this Tribunal which have presented sufficient information about this point, and this has been submitted to the evaluation of the Judges, and, therefore, I believe that today we should not lose any more time -- or spend more time, if you will, on the various questions in this vein. I believe that the decision by this Tribunal is again undisputable. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, regarding the question of testimony on a model of behaviour of the accused, we have reached a point when there may be an inequality of arms between the Defence and the Prosecution. Why? We have tried to prove and we wish to prove a certain model of behaviour of the accused throughout their life, and in accordance with certain rules, that is, Rule 93 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The Prosecutor is calling in question the need of presenting evidence under that Rule and is proposing, at the same time, and this is being accepted by the Trial Chamber, that evidence be presented in the form of the testimony of the wife of the former Ambassador Galbraith, who speaks about a completely different location with a different profile of the population, and is trying, by analogy, to transpose the situation there to the situation in Ahmici. Therefore, it is our submission that if we do not hear testimony about a model of behaviour, then we need not hear the testimony of the former -- of the wife of the former Ambassador, which relates to a village distant from Vitez and Ahmici in which the population is absolutely rural, a rather isolated environment as opposed to Ahmici, which is a suburb of Vitez, and which all the population was employed in the factory, in industry. So these are entirely different milieuxs and yet they are being used to make analogies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I shall be very brief. The fact that you feel that it is unnecessary to call witnesses who will testify about the character of the accused will put us in a situation as to be unable to discuss some factual matters, because those witnesses also speak about certain facts which are outside the framework of character, namely, the Prosecutor in his opening statement and in the Pre-Trial brief in several places underlined that the motives for the behaviour of the accused in the 16th, he finds in their nationalist and extremist views. Through character witnesses we are trying to prove that these persons never behaved in that manner, that they never thought along those lines, that they were not members of any political parties, nor did they demonstrate any such positions. Therefore, this is a part of our defence, and I think that we will need either through evidence on models of behaviour or to call those witnesses as fact witnesses in order to hear them describe these matters for your benefit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before we move on, can I clarify one point. When this morning I was talking about character witnesses, of course I was referring to the witnesses we heard the last two weeks who were fact witnesses testifying about specific facts relating to Count 1 and who in passing -- but this took a lot of time. They were also questioned about the character of the accused. They all consistently said that the accused were good neighbours, nice people, friendly, good workers. They took part in circles, groups and so on, and without any aggressive behaviour. So the point, first of all, is that therefore what I said this morning was only referring to fact witnesses, and my appeal was to try to refrain from asking questions to these witnesses about the character of the accused. This has nothing to do with the character witnesses proper. This is a question we had already discussed, and on that matter we had asked to apply Rule 94 ter. You may remember. We have already tackled this matter a few weeks ago when we asked the Defence counsel to try to submit affidavits relating to those character witnesses, affidavits. That means that at least one character witness could be called here in Court, one for each accused, of course, plus we would have the production of affidavits. And I remember that on that occasion I asked the Prosecutor whether the Prosecution was agreeable, and Mr. Terrier said, well, we will decide on it by a case-by-case basis. So we can't in advance say that we will accept all the affidavits. As I said, this is a separate matter which relates only to character witnesses. We are now discussing the issue of fact witnesses, and the appeal was to try to set time -- the appeal of the Court to try to save time by simply refraining from asking questions which, and this is my second point, are repetitive, because we always listen to the same response, which is always the same. They are good, they were good people, they are good people, they behaved very well and so on. Since the Prosecution is not contesting this point, we don't see why we should spend hours and hours listening always to the same statements. These are the two points I wanted to make. As for the model of behaviour, I think, with all due respect, Rule 93 on pattern of conduct is not relevant to that. It's not relevant because I think I was part of the drafting -- I took some part in the drafting of this Rule 93, and I can tell you this consistent pattern of conduct was -- this rule was conceived of as relating to crimes against humanity. When you may have to prove the existence of a consistent practice or systematic practice, I don't see why and what extent Rule 93 could relate to the issue of character. Not the issue of persecution. In that respect it may be relevant. But it's a different issue. Now, we are discussing the question of the character of the accused. So therefore I would submit that 93 is not relevant. But let us now move on. I wonder whether Counsel Pavkovic could react to the proposals made by the Prosecutor about Zagreb as the possible place. Counsel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence of Vladimir Santic accepts with satisfaction this reasonable proposal by the Prosecution. However, I am faced with the organisational task. So I cannot say, as of this moment, whether this meeting can be held on the 20th. So I beg for understanding. But in principle I do accept this proposal to mutual satisfaction, and we are pleased that the Prosecutor has understanding for our suggestion. As for the technical side of it, I don't wish to tire you with those details, but I will inform the Prosecution in due course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I am sure that the Prosecutor will make it possible. And they will negotiate with you also on the dates, probably, if you have problems, the date can be put off. Probably not on the 20th, but the following week. I don't know. I hope both parties will reach an agreement also on the details concerning the date of the interviews. Mr. Terrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am happy that Mr. Pavkovic has accepted the proposal I have just made. We will make efforts to agree upon a date and I hope that we will be able to inform this Tribunal very soon of the results of these discussions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. I apologise for referring very briefly, once again, to the previous matter. If I understood well, and that is why I am asking for the floor, regarding the presentation of evidence regarding the character of the accused. Maybe I misunderstood, and I shall be glad to be corrected. I think that what we have discussed does not exclude entirely the presentation of evidence regarding the character of the accused. And my understanding is based on the fact that I believe that some evidence, such as in the case of our client, the accused Vlatko Kupreskic, which we intend to present, is not such as to be a burden for these proceedings. What I mean is that we have a couple of witnesses who are Muslim by nationality, and we believe that their testimony about the behaviour of our client, and these witnesses are also victims of the conflict that occurred in 1993, and we feel that it would be useful for a fair and lawful determination for the Trial Chamber to hear the testimony of those two or possibly three witnesses of Muslim ethnicity. Therefore, my question is whether the ruling made by the Trial Chamber a moment ago excludes calling in this particular case one or two Muslim witnesses to testify to this matter, because we consider this to be significant for our defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Krajina, the Trial Chamber agrees with you. The two or three character witnesses you intend to call should be called and will be called here, because they, as I said, they are not fact witnesses. They will be character witnesses and you attach particular importance to their testimony. I imagine they will not repeat what we have been hearing so far. There will be no repetitious evidence. And so therefore they are fully admissible. What we are against is the repetitive character of some evidence about the personality of the accused. So there should be no doubt in your mind, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I think we should now move on because it's high time for us to bring in the next witness. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blaz. Will you please introduce yourself to the Court and give us the fundamental data about yourself, your name, place of residence, date of birth, place of birth.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Good morning. My name is Zeljko Blaz. I was born in Travnik on the 14th of December, 1964.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you live?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: My permanent place of residence is Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you were employed before the war?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I was employed in the Princip factory in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Until 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you made redundant or did you resign your job?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, I was made redundant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you find a job after that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: After that I started working in Caritas at the parish office in Vitez, at the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Caritas was established by the parish office; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, by the parish office that is by the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What area did the Vitez Caritas cover?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: The municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court to whom did the Caritas offer help in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Caritas, as we all know, is an organisation and we provided help to all those who were imperilled, who were at risk, to old-age pensioners, the elderly, persons who needed homecare, all those who needed assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you help refugees?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What number of refugees are we referring to at that time who passed through your system of assistance?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: In the first half of 1992 there were fewer refugees, but there was a larger wave of refugees in the second half of 1992. Mostly from Kotor Varos and Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us any figures? Can you say something about the numbers.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: There were about 7.000 refugees at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them were Muslims, how many Croats?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Well, about 5.000 Muslims and about 2.000 Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Caritas involved in finding accommodation for these people, helping them to find accommodation?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Caritas offer assistance to Muslims and Croats in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Caritas also help Muslim refugees as well as Croatian refugees?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. It helped all refugees and all people, regardless of their ethnicity or religion. There was no distinction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any other organisation established in the Vitez area in 1992, in the second half of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Well, we started operating in the beginning of 1992. In mid-1992, Merhamet was established in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the founder of Merhamet?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I think the Islamic community. This was a religious organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the UNHCR active on the territory of the Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. The UNHCR was active in the second half of the year, and actually at that time there was an office in Vitez and they had a warehouse in Prahulje, in the direction of Travnik. They were active in Vitez until the -- and of October, and then they moved to Zenica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the economic conditions in 1992, early 1993, did they worsen? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they worsened noticeably. People were unemployed and there was more and more need for humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period after the founding of Merhamet, did Caritas continue to help both Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. Caritas helped all before Merhamet was established and after it was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Caritas also help people remaining in the Vitez municipality after the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people who remained there and were Muslims by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this go on?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: This went on -- well, from the beginning to the end, almost. Throughout this time, we helped all the people living in Vitez, whether they were Muslim or Croat or Serbian, both before the war and during the war and after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, conflict started in the Vitez municipality and the Muslims who were there were cut off from Merhamet; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: That's correct. They all went over to your side. All the Muslims who were in Vitez at that time used to come to Caritas, where they were given help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other way that welfare could be provided for them, apart from Caritas, at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: During the war? No. I think that at that time, they were entirely supported by Caritas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many families you were looking after at the end of the war? I'm referring to Muslim families.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: About 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at these documents. This is only a brief selection, so can you describe the way this assistance was provided very briefly, and by what means.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (No microphone).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I wonder whether the registrar could again tell us the number of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just have a look: This is about the assistance of the parish Caritas of Vitez which was sent to the humanitarian organisation Merhamet. And the dates are different; there is one document from 1992, another from 1993, and further on in 1993, I think the last one we have here is from July 1993. So can you tell us how this assistance was delivered?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: This is how it was. We gave help in an organised way, but also on an individual basis. So whoever came to us to ask for aid was given aid. Apart from this, when I say in an organised manner, I am referring to old-age pensioners, according to the list we received from the pension fund, and we helped all the old-age pensioners in the Vitez municipality. These documents here, which I'm very familiar with, because I signed them all and I issued them, show that regardless of this way of helping, we also gave assistance to Merhamet as an organisation so that they could forward this to those who needed it. In the same way, there is a firefighting organisation here. We know that firemen are very important for a municipality, and since they were not paid at that time, we provided assistance to them as well. Because the firefighters were not paid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the last of these receipts dates from July 1993, and it refers to aid given to local Muslim families. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you signed all these receipts?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court whether these are the only receipts that were issued? Were these the only cases where aid was given, or was there much more?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, these are only some of the many more receipts that exist, because this period in which we helped all people lasted much longer than can be seen from these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court whether, apart from this aid in food and clothing which was provided as can be seen here, whether there was also a pharmacy with medicaments that were donated.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, there was a pharmacy which operated in the same way as the parish Caritas. It was, in fact, called the Caritas pharmacy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it issue medicine to Muslims in the same way as it did to Croats?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Even in one period in late 1992 and early 1993, many more Muslims came to the pharmacy than Croats did. There were persons who worked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this go on during the war?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. No distinction was made either before or during or after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one more question: Can you say whether anyone tried to influence Caritas in any way, or to influence you as the head of this organisation, to prevent you from giving help to Muslims or to reduce that help before or during the war?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, there was no attempt to influence me. When I started working, this was one of the conditions: I was to have total freedom in my work, and in deciding -- in agreement with others, but my decision was final, and there was to be no outside influence into my work -- on my work. So there was no influence by anyone on the work of Caritas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Either by political or military bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Blaz. I have finished. I would just like to ask that D80/2 be taken into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So it is admitted into evidence. Is any other Defence counsel going to examine in chief or cross-examine this witness? Mr. Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have only one question; I would like to clarify one point. Re-examined by Mr. Pavkovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Blaz, I am Counsel Petar Pavkovic. You stated that Caritas was established by the parish office. You also stated that Caritas made no distinction in giving aid with reference to ethnicity or religion, that you helped Muslims and Muslim refugees also. I would just like to ask you, since there were various religious community, is Caritas Catholic? Did it belong to a Catholic religious organisation?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: That's all. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will also be very short. Cross-examined by Mr. Terrier:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, my name is Franck Terrier. I am one of the members of the Prosecution. I would like to ask you very briefly a number of questions about Caritas. It seems that -- I seem to have understood from what you said that Caritas, for which you worked at that time in the Vitez area, was affiliated with Caritas International, which is a humanitarian organisation based on Roman Catholicism; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, we were affiliated to other Caritas organisations. We were in contact with them as far as this was possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regardless of the extent of this relation, you respected their general guidelines with regards to the actions of Caritas International throughout the world or throughout conflicts during which it may intervene?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I simply wish to know, sir, whether you considered at the time that you had to comply with the general rules or regulations governing Caritas International throughout the world and throughout all conflicts during which this Catholic international organisation would be called upon to act.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: This is how it was. "Caritas" means giving to all people and help to all people who need help. And we were led by this, regardless of ethnicity, religion, or anything else, absolutely without any kind of prejudice. Which means that -- the very word "Caritas" means giving to all people without any distinctions among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me in saying that the principle of nondiscrimination is a fundamental principle of all international humanitarian organisations and in all countries in which these organisations are called upon to act?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned the arrival of 5.000 Muslim refugees in the municipality of Vitez during the second trimester of 1992. Would you please specify how many of these 5.000 Muslim refugees the office of Caritas, for which you worked, aided during the course of that time period and the following time period: That is to say in the course of the year 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: This is how it was. Since we made no distinction among people when helping them, we did not make any distinction in the numbers as to whom we helped most. Whoever came, regardless of whether they were a Muslim refugee or a Catholic refugee or any other, they were helped, and of course we had to keep a record of the amounts given so that we would know how much we had in our warehouse. But we didn't pay much attention to the numbers of the various kinds of people who came to Caritas. And there were a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Caritas office for which you worked have relations with the civilian authorities and military authorities who were Croats in the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Caritas had relation with the civilian authorities in the sense that in contacts, if we needed help, in vehicles, in fuel, in any other way, and we were unable to get this for ourselves but we needed it for our work, because we didn't have the means to get all that for ourselves. And this is the only reason why we contacted the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1993, did the Caritas office visit, for example, the school in Dubravica, where there were Muslims detained?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Caritas office not consider that this was a mission that was within its area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: The Caritas office was not aware of what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other humanitarian organisations were intervening at the same time in that area, aside from Caritas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Are you referring to international organisations as well?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now speaking of all humanitarian organisations represented in the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. Caritas was the first organisation which started working in the Vitez municipality. We were the first to organise, and of course as such we were the first to start giving aid. Then, in the second half of the year, as I have already stated, Merhamet was established. There was also the Red Cross. There was an organisation called "Mother and Child." Of the international organisations which had their offices in Vitez, there was the UNHC after a brief period of time, and I think "Feed the Children." There was also "Premiere Ogesse." (phoen)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question, sir. Getting back to the Muslims who were detained in the Dubravica school in April, it seems that the Red Cross intervened in that school. How can you explain that the Red Cross was informed of the detention of Muslims in the Dubravica school and not Caritas?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Caritas was distributing food, and the Red Cross -- it's logical that the Red Cross should be informed of such things if they existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Re-examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, Mr. Terrier has asked you about the principles of Caritas and international humanitarian organisations, one of which was called Caritas. Were those principles implemented by you in practice?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that Merhamet was founded in the second half of 1992, which is also a humanitarian organisation guided by the principle of assisting everyone.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Merhamet extend aid to Croats? Are you aware of any single such case?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I think not. At least I am not aware of any such case. All the aid that we received and which we stored in our warehouses was distributed very shortly after being received, and this went on continuously. As soon as aid arrived it would be distributed and then we would wait for the next delivery, so that the people who needed aid most would receive that aid almost daily or at small intervals, so that they didn't need to go anywhere else to seek assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the foundation of Merhamet, was the burden reduced for Caritas because Merhamet was giving relief to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I think so, because when we started operating most people would come to us. It was only natural that once Merhamet was founded this would ease the burden on Caritas, though people did come even after Merhamet was founded, they still came to Caritas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they received aid?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why the UNHCR left Vitez? Are you aware of the reasons?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I am sorry that they stayed for such a short while in Vitez, and I asked why they were leaving, and they said that they were leaving for either some security or some other reasons. In my opinion, there was no reason for them to leave, but they probably knew more than I about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know remember when they left?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I think at the end of October 1992 or the beginning of November roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who founded -- who actually founded the Vitez Caritas? Could you give us the name and the parish office?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Brother Blazevic, Bozidar Blazevic the parish priest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also tell the Trial Chamber whether the refugees, and you said at a certain point in time 7.000 of them had reached Vitez, were the Croatian refugees assisted by Caritas to leave Vitez? Do you know anything about those efforts?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. Most Croatian displaced persons spent a very short time in Vitez. They were assisted by -- of course, respecting the wish of each individual to live where he wants and to go where he wants. We did not try to influence them in any way. They were there for a short while, they were given relief and then they left in search of better conditions and a better life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the Muslim refugees?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: The majority of the Muslims, displaced Muslims, stayed on in our area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We have no questions, so thank you so much for coming to testify in court. You may now be released. Thank you, Mr. Blaz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, are you requesting any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So we will bring in the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Before hearing this witness, Your Honour, I should like to say that this witness will testify about a region adjoining Ahmici, Loncari and Putis villages, and this testimony refers to the testimony of Major Matthew Woolley. The Prosecutor has already presented evidence about the circumstances in that area, and that is why we are going back to it now. So these are events that the Prosecutor has already presented evidence about. So we will present the events there from our standpoint. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you tell us your name and your particulars, where you were born, when and where you live now?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: My name is Anto Plavcic. I was born on the 22nd of August, 1954 in Jelinak, Busovaca municipality, the former state of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are you living now?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I'm now living in the municipality of Busovaca. You can speed up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher for his assistance to show this map to the witness, please, and Their Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D81/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Plavcic, will you please look at this map? It's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: May I use this pointer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but on the ELMO. Not on the screen, over there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I see now, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the court, please, where you were living in 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Ever since my birth until 1993, I lived in a place called Jelinak. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which are the larger towns close to the place?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Putis, Loncari, Bakije, and these are on the slopes of Mount Kuber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distance between these villages, Jelinak, Loncari, Putis?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: From Jelinak to Putis the distance is one kilometre, from Jelinak to Loncari again about one kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do those villages even touch on the fringes?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: There are a few scattered houses linking them together. Loncari and Jelinak are separated by this cemetery here, so there may be empty space between them of about 400 to 500 metres. I couldn't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The ethnic composition of Jelinak was 50 per cent, or, rather, half/half Croats and Muslims. There were no other ethnic groups in Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big was the village? How many houses were there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Jelinak numbered about 100 households, which means that about 50 of them were Muslim and about 50 Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The size of Putis and the ethnic composition of Putis?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Putis is slightly smaller. It has about 80 households, I think. Roughly about 80. About 30 per cent of those are Croat, 20 to 30 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the village of Loncari?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The village of Loncari, again there were between 70 and 80 households. Loncari was inhabited by Muslims but there were several Serb or orthodox households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there's also the village of Bakije in that region, and who were the inhabitants of that village?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The village of Bakije was inhabited exclusively by Croats and there were about 20 households. About 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those villages are on the slopes of Mount Kuber, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the village of Bakije is, as we can see, a bit further removed. There is another hill there called Gradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the distance between those villages and the village of Ahmici? Could you show us Ahmici on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes. Here, this is where Ahmici is. The distance was about -- from Jelinak it was about four to five kilometres, like this, but this was the road that had to be used. So along the road it may be about seven kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So prior to the outbreak of the war in that region you were living in Jelinak, and what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, there is no translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you hear? We could not. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can Your Honours hear us now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what you were doing before the war.

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Before the war, I was working in the Mediapan factory as a tool-maker. In the Mediapan company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it located?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: In Busovaca. Actually, Mediapan is in Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you working all the time or were you laid off for a while?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: When the conflicts and disturbances started I was not working really. I went to the company now and then, but mostly I wasn't working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a member of the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a representative of the Civil Defence in the Katici local community, and I was the representative for Jelinak on behalf of the Civil Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not a military conscript?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: No, I was not, ever since 1972 when I regulated my status.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are disabled, that is the reason, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell the Trial Chamber what happened in 1993 in your area? Do you remember who had control of the features and the peaks of Kuber?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: In 1993, members of the Croatian Defence Council had control of Kuber, but in this area here there were members of the BH army, that is, to the northeast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about relations in the village, were there members of the HVO, of the TO, and the BiH Army in the village?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: In 1993 there were members of the HVO in the village and there were also members of the Territorial Defence, or the BiH Army. Relations in 1993 were strained, so that there were few contacts between the two and relations cooled after the shelling of Busovaca, so that these people separated from us. They didn't wish to work with us any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So relations worsened after the conflict in Busovaca in January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, do you know who held control of Kuber on that day and whether anything unusual happened in that area, in view of the fact that this was in your immediate vicinity?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, I was at home in the morning. We could hear shooting in the Kuber area, so that this was something surprising, something unusual, and we wondered what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fire started around noon. Did it go on all day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The shooting went on until nightfall with different degrees of intensity, and in the afternoon two members of the HVO were wounded and they were evacuated via Jelinak in the direction of Kaonik. In the direction of Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were those wounded HVO members?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The first one was called Slavko Jelic, and the other one was Dragan Andrijasevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they inhabitants of Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes. Both of them were living in Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were HVO members?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them being evacuated via Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, because we were all frightened by the shooting, we went to see what was going on, and when they appeared and the other people who came to carry them and to evacuate them and save them, we saw them, and they went via Jelinak through the pass in the direction of Kaonik and the hospital there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the positions on Kuber were held by the HVO, and that positions near Kicina were held by the BiH Army?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the first to attack or, rather, who were the combatants?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of April I don't know who attacked whom, because I wasn't there, I was in the village, and who was the one to carry out the attack. But when these people were evacuated, we heard that the HVO was attacked by the army from the direction of Zenica. Here. Somewhere here. Yes. Along here (indicating). And from these directions. In any event, from Zenica, the HVO had been attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fighting that was going on in the vicinity of the village, was anything happening in the surrounding villages in Putis, Loncari; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: As far as Putis is concerned, there were fewer Croats there, and when the shooting was heard, those people got scared and fled to Jelinak. Not all of them. Some of them. So that they sought shelter here and in the evening of the 15th they stayed with relatives and friends, some of them, while others fled without knowing where they should go. Anyway, they took the road towards Kaonik, Saretovici and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 15th the fighting started. Did they continue onto the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The fighting lapsed in the night of the 15th and then in the morning of the 16th the fighting gained in intensity, increasingly throughout the area of Kuber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the shooting heard?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: In the area of Saracevac. There was no fighting here (indicating), there was just shooting from one side. The fighting was going on in this area of Kuber here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any shooting directed at the village?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 16th. On the 16th, yes, fire started to be directed towards the village. First from this direction here, from Kicin, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you've shown us that. Fine.

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: So that is when the village was exposed to fire in the morning. Shells hit the Croatian part of the village of Jelinak. There were mortar shells. You can't really tell where they come from, but you can hear them coming from here, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's another arrow here from Merdani. Was there any shelling from that direction, do you recollect?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon there was fire coming from the direction of Merdani, from this direction here and here, from Vran Stijena.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the village was in a sense surrounded, and the only free passage was towards Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes. Along this road towards Kaonik, but these people from Vran Stijena can see most of this road leading to Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that the Croatian part of the village was shelled. How was that village divided?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: It was divided in such a way that the upper part of the village, because the village is on a slope, the ground is not flat, so on the higher part of the village there were Muslim houses and at the lower level the Croatian houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th did the rest of the Croats come from Putis?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes, the rest of the Croats came from Putis to Jelinak saying that they were exposed to shelling from the direction of Kicin. This I am showing you the arrow now. So that these people arrived terrified and passed through Jelinak and fled in the direction of Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear where the fighting was going on? Was the frontline shift that they --

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Well, the shooting intensified and came closer on the 15th, and the 16th, in the morning, fighting took place along the top of Kuber, while on the 16th, in the afternoon, the fighting came closer to the village and the intensity of the shelling increased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people start leaving Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes, the people from Jelinak fled together with these other people in the direction of Kaonik as well. They fled. In the afternoon shelling started, but I already described that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 17th of April, when did everyone leave the village?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Well, on the 17th there had been fighting all night. It grew less in the early morning hours, about 1.00, 2.00, 3.00 a.m. When dawn broke the shooting came closer and those who had not fled already started to flee because there was more and more shelling against -- on the village from heavy artillery from the direction of Kicin and these other two directions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel, shall I propose that we take a break now? Thank you. Thirty-minute break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: (No translation)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Again, we have no translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: (No translation)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Testing. Can you hear us now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the technicians hear us on this channel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: (No translation)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Hello. Can you hear the translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: You can now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We were talking about the 17th of April. What happened next? You said that the civilians were leaving?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 17th of April in the early hours the shooting became less intense, but it was closer, as we said, so it was near, as we said. But in the early morning hours it was less intense. On the 17th in the early morning hours the shooting then became more intense and reached a climax. It was like hell. They were shooting from all the directions I have mentioned on the entire village of Jelinak, which was inhabited by Croats. So they were shooting from Vran Stijena.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that the fighting was in the immediate vicinity of the village?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the early morning hours the fighting got very, very close and it was terrible. It was dreadful. It was terrible shelling, shooting from machine guns and the population was in a panic and they were fleeing in the direction of Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Did the entire Croatian population leave on that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Before noon the entire civilian population left, all the civilians from the village of Jelinak, but two elderly men stayed behind. One was killed, the other was wounded later here near the cemetery, near the cemetery, because a shell fell, and one of them lost part of his leg and the other one was killed. We continued fleeing in the direction of Kaonik. When we arrived there and had to cross the bridge to the village of Saretovici, in this spot from the direction of Merdani here, there was shooting from heavy machine gun in our direction, and when we came here near Saretovici, there was no shooting at us any more, and we could hear the shelling from behind us. As I have already said, there was intense fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that they were shooting from the direction of Merdani when you were fleeing as civilians. Who was in Merdani?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Merdani was a purely Muslim village. There were no Croats in Merdani. Above Merdani there was one or two -- there were one or two Serbian houses. What happened to these people, whether they had already left or whether they stayed, I don't know. I don't know what happened in Merdani. I only know when we were passing along this part of the road, there was shooting at us from this direction with a heavy machine gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Bakije is here. Did the Croats from Bakije stay there or did they flee too?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The Croats from Bakije also fled, but they were not with us. However, they arrived in Busovaca on that day because this machine gun from Merdani and the other one from the direction of Zarac. On the 15th or the 16th -- on the 15th there was one, on the 16th there was another machine gun, and from Zarac, and they were able to shoot at this part of the Croatian village of Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Considering the fact that, obviously, Croatian villages, or parts of villages were being shot at, could you see that there was any advance by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: We couldn't see it, but we heard, because the shooting was coming close so fast when they started shooting from Vran Stijena. It means that they were moving, and they were following in the direction in which we were fleeing. So the shooting got close to the very edge of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court when the HVO left this area since you went to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 17th, in the afternoon, we arrived in Busovaca and we were accommodated with family friends, holiday houses which were empty. We were accommodated there by members of the civil defence and the Red Cross on the 17th. On the 18th we heard that there was fierce fighting in the village of Jelinak itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you heard that apart from the fighting in Jelinak, what other villages were caught in the fighting? Where was the line?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 18th there was a line in the village of Loncari as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you say the HVO withdrew?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 18th, the HVO withdrew. The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina took over the village of Jelinak completely, so that the HVO retreated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the 18th, since then, has this entire area been under the control first of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and then of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. So from the 18th of April, 1993, the village of Jelinak, the village of Bakija, Putis, have been totally under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and now of the Muslims. So the Muslims have come back to the villages of Loncari, Jelinak; they never left Putis. But the Croats have not returned either to Bakije or Jelinak. In 1998, the Croats returned to the village of Gavrine Kuce. This was in late autumn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was also abandoned by the Croats earlier?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it had been abandoned earlier, and seven Croatian houses now have been reinhabited since late autumn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the Croatian houses in this area? Were the Croatian houses in Jelinak, Putis, Bakija, left intact, or were they set on fire?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 18th, in the afternoon, when we learned that the village of Jelinak was completely under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we heard that all the houses had been set on fire, burnt down, and that the HVO had no access there. I personally -- I think it was in 1995 -- I visited the cemetery for All Saints' Day, and I managed to come to my house in the village of Jelinak with a police escort, and escorted -- escorted by the HVO police and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I saw that all the houses except for two houses had been burnt down, destroyed, including my house. And the Muslim houses --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about these two houses?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: These two houses had a roof on. There were windows. I don't know what state they were in inside, but I know that they had roofs and windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 19th, the 18th or the 19th, this area was abandoned completely by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes, the HVO left. As far as I heard, the HVO retreated, and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina took complete control over this area. This line at Loncari, which passed through Loncari, was held by the HVO, but the rest was fully controlled by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Court has heard a witness who said that on the 25th of April of 1993, he was in the village of Jelinak, and that this village had been burnt; however, he considered that this had been done by the HVO. Do you know whether there were any other incidents after the 19th of April, 1993, which might have led to the destruction of these houses?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: After the 17th, in the morning, when I left the village with those civilians who were still there, except for the two who stayed behind, I don't know what happened afterwards. But I do know that early in the morning on the 17th, above this upper part of the village, because it has a lower part and an upper part, in the early morning hours you could see a light, so it's probable that something was burning there. But I wasn't there, so I can't say what was burning and who had set it on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This witness also said that he saw pigs that had been killed in the village which had been burnt, and that this left a very bad impression. Who had kept pigs in the village?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Well, in the village of Jelinak it was the Croats who kept pigs. The Muslims never kept pigs, as far as I know. And I have heard that they never had pigs, and I know that Muslims don't keep pigs. They don't keep pigs today, either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the Croatian houses in Putis?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The Croatian houses in Putis were all set on fire. I heard this was done on the 18th when the HVO retreated. When the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina took over control of this territory completely, we were in Busovaca, and we heard that all the houses in Putis had been set alight, like the ones in Jelinak, except for the two I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the houses in Bakija?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The houses in Bakija were also set on fire, but I don't know exactly when, whether it was on the 18th or later. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: In any case, they have all been completely burnt, and I have not returned to my house yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have finished. I would like to ask the Court to accept D81/2 as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Any other Defence counsel? Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. No other Defence counsel has the intention to question this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Blaxill:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Plavcic. My name is Michael Blaxill. I'm one of the prosecutors in this case, and I do have a few questions I would like to ask you as a result of the evidence you've given this morning. Now, you said that the Kuber area was under the control of the HVO prior to April of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: That is right. It is true that HVO members were in the area, in the area of Kuber. But in this part, there were members of the TO; in fact, the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the village of Jelinak, is it not the case that in January of 1993, there was a demand by the local HVO that the Muslims should disarm and rely upon the protection of the HVO in the region? Do you recall that happening?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I do not recall that, because I'm a civilian, and I was not familiar with those military information, and I don't know what was happening, no, nor that that was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later on, at around the 15th of April, before the heavy fighting, do you recall the detention of Muslim males in the village who were removed from the village that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 15th? On the 15th, there were no detentions. I don't know. As far as I know, no one was taken in detention. The Muslims were in their part of the village; we were in ours. But both were scared, both they and us, when we heard the shooting in the area of Kuber, and especially when these two men, Slavko and Dragan, arrived in the village wounded, and when they were transferred to Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that on or before the 15th of April, you do not recall the removal of any Muslim males from the village of Jelinak? Just to be certain, that's what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I don't know of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had worked in Kaonik, you knew the place; were you aware of a subsequent detention centre that was set there in which Muslims were detained in some numbers?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I worked in the factory called Mediapan that was situated right here. That is the company's name, Mediapan. In the area of Saretovici, there was a barracks where the army was quartered. And I know of no other place that could be used as detention, for detention purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently hear anything about Muslims being detained in a facility at Kaonik camp?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in Busovaca, we were fleeing towards Busovaca, and when we reached Busovaca, we heard that some Muslims -- how many and who, I don't know -- were detained in the Kaonik prison, in the barracks in Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on and about the 15th of April, is it true that the HVO forces on Kuber had become engaged in military action against the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I don't know what was happening at Kuber on the 15th. All I know is that the shooting fell silent. And as the HVO held positions here, and the BH Army here, in this area, on the 15th, occasionally a machine gun shelled the village of Jelinak, and there was fighting on a smaller scale in the area of Kuber. But on the 16th, another machine gun was heard firing from this direction towards Jelinak and Bakija and Putis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could now turn attention for a moment to the village of Loncari: Do you recall what happened there on the 26th of January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: 26th of January? I don't know. I have no idea what happened in Loncari on the 26th. Actually, I don't know what was happening in general in Loncari, because I was in Jelinak. That's far away. There's a small pass here, and my house is a bit lower down there, so that I couldn't see the village of Loncari, nor did I know what was happening there. But when we were fleeing, we passed by Loncari. The Loncari were on our right as we fled towards Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicate that these villages are, on the map, fairly close to one another; did you not at around that date in late January hear of shelling and shooting in the region of Loncari?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: The village of Loncari? There was no shooting or shelling of Loncari in January. There was no shooting at Jelinak. There was no shooting at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I turn to the village of Putis, would you say the same there, that there was no gunfire heard in that place in late January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: There was no gunfire from Putis or Jelinak. There was no gunfire in January. Gunfire was heard over here, in the direction of Merdani. These hills and mountains here, Crna and towards Lasva, Kula, in the Kula area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I would say to you, Mr. Plavcic, that before another chamber there have been witnesses who stated that both Putis and Loncari received fire from the HVO in late January, would you say that was wrong?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Ms. Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have an objection, because not a single witness said that in this Trial Chamber. There were comments about April, but there were no witnesses who spoke about January 1993. So I think the Prosecutor was not correct in mentioning this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm referring in fact to evidence in another Chamber, and I'm just putting the factual proposition as to whether the witness agrees or disagrees with that factual proposition. It would be a matter for rebuttal at the end of the day if that were of such significance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not aware of this, and the defence does not know that any witness made such a statement in another Trial Chamber. If the Prosecutor wishes to ask this witness about January, let him ask him directly, without introducing the testimony of any other witnesses of which we are not aware. So I think he can ask the question directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I think Counsel Slokovic-Glumacvic is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will rephrase the question to avoid further debate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time yourself hear of such shelling ever taking place in late January and targeting Loncari or Putis?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: There was no shelling that I know of. I really don't know that there was any shelling in that area. There was no shelling, no gunfire here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at any time, hear of the roundup of any Muslim males in those two villages on or before the 15th of April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've referred to the intensity of fighting, and there was clearly a substantial attack on Kuber by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina against the HVO on the 16th of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. There was gunfire and fighting on the 16th. They were more intense than on the 15th because from the direction of Kicin, Zarac, tromedza and Vran Stijena, they were shelling the Croatian part of the village of Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting then that there was no damage to the Muslim part of the village of Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: On the 16th there was no damage, only on the 17th in the morning hours I saw, in the upper part of the village, the Muslim part of the village, that something was on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, would it -- to the best of your knowledge, Mr. Plavcic, wasn't there, in fact, just the area becoming a large battle zone with damage to both Croatian and Muslim properties?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: That is correct, that on the 18th all houses in the village of Jelinak and Putis, in Putis the Croatian houses and in the village of Jelinak all the houses, were burning on the 18th. That is what I heard in Busovaca, that all the houses were on fire. Which were the ones to start burning first, I don't know. As far as I saw, it was the upper part of the village, in the early morning hours, that started burning first in the village of Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac? Re-examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
