utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see, you yourself, any Muslims being taken away from the village on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I did not see that. I do know that later some Muslims were detained in the Kaonik Prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone was taken from the village on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I do not know who was taken nor whether anyone was taken. We heard that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding Kuber, you said that it's a hill which represents a border between three municipalities, Vitez, Busovaca, and Zenica, and it was held by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: There's a place called Lug where the borders of the three municipalities meet and it was held by the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you could hear the fighting from Kuber, would the HVO attack anyone on Kuber as the HVO already had control of Kuber?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: I really don't know whom they could attack up there, I just know that there was gunfire. I don't know who they attacked, because on the other side of Kuber were more distant villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. They were held by the BH army. But Kuber was under the control of the Croatian forces at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO PLAVCIC
utterances.text: As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We have no questions. Mr. Plavcic, thank you so much for testifying before the Court. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Puliselic, I wonder whether you are requesting any protective measures for the three witnesses you're going to call.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: We're not requesting any protective measures. I would just like to make an observation, Your Honours, and that is to say that the next witness is, at the same time, a witness for Vlatko Kupreskic's defence, so I would ask the Defence counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic to be treated on an equal footing as me, only regarding certain aspects of the case, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So I assume, therefore, this witness will be examined-in-chief by yourself and by Counsel Krajina is what you meant. Yes? Good. Thank you. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vidovic. Good morning. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Puliselic. Examined by Mr. Puliselic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please introduce yourself to Their Honours, your name, where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Ivo Vidovic. I was born on the 11th of June, 1944, in the village of Pirici, Vitez municipality. I am now living in the village of Santici, Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please tell us what your occupation is?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a private entrepreneur, a restaurateur in catering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is your catering establishment?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the village of Santici, a place called Zume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it in your own home?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in my own home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we place an aerial photograph of Ahmici on the easel, please? I think it was Prosecution Exhibit number 2. Mr. Vidovic, behind your back you see the easel with an aerial photograph of Ahmici, and I should like to ask you kindly to find your house on that photograph and to point it out to us.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the Busovaca-Vitez road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it could be put on the other side.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, I have only asked you to show us your house.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is on the Busovaca-Vitez main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you point it out to us?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the name of that part of the settlement?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Village of Santici, settlement of Zume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may be seated now. Who were your immediate neighbours?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean among the Croats or the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My closest neighbour is Anto Vidosevic. Then there's Marko Livancic, Jozo Lovric and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And among the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among the Muslims my closest was (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was his house from yours?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: About 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there others?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Across the main road there were quite a number of neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your relationships were with the Muslims before the war?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Exceptionally good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you assist them on certain occasions?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions. We were so close that I helped them on a number of occasions. I helped them and they helped me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did that help consist of?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me see. In every way we helped each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us generally, what were relations like between the Croats and Muslims in Ahmici before the war?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Extremely good. We exchanged visits, on religious holidays we visited them, and they came to visit us on our holidays and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you know generally about the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, I know that the aggression started against Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Serbs or the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning did the Croats and Muslims participate on the same side in the struggle against the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally engaged in the fighting against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My son went on a number of occasions and I went once, voluntarily, near Travnik on the slopes of Mount Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly, but roughly the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was on the foot of Mount Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were a volunteer?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend there, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time I was there for four or five days, together with my son, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the battles there, did the Muslims participate together with the Croats?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This unit of yours, the one you joined, did it have a name? What was its name?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time we organised ourselves on a voluntary basis. There was no formality. There weren't any uniforms even. We wore civilian clothes. One or two of us may have had a camouflage jacket, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after returning from Vlasic what did you do?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We, the locals in the village, organised ourselves to keep watch duty in the village. We organised village guard duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you participate often in guard duty?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we changed. We took turns in groups. A group of us would keep watch one night and another group the next night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of your village, did you keep guard duty jointly at first?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did, both us and the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that guard duty?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The purpose -- since Serb units would break into the village at night, so we tried to protect the village from such incursions. We were afraid of the infiltration of terrorists into the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start keeping watch duty separately?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This started, I think -- I cannot remember exactly, but as local people, I think we separated after the first Muslim-Croat conflict in the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the immediate cause, in your view, of that separation? Was it the multi-party elections or something else?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Immediately after the multi-party elections people started to split along ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did military structures organise those village guards or not?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how did they come about? Who organised them?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We, the local villagers, got together and realised we needed to keep watch duty because of those incursions of terrorists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a person who was in command of those village guards?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In our village, in the village of Santici and Zume, Nenad Santic was in charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to Nenad Santic? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nenad Santic was killed. I know that he was ambushed by some Muslim units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly when that took place?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in the middle or the end of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself as guards select Nenad Santic as your commander?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how -- what kind of weapons you had?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There were a number of hunters in the village, so these were mostly hunting rifles. Some people had licences to carry weapons, some had pistols. There were a couple of M48 rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a military rifle?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally have a rifle?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guards wear uniforms in your village?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. One or two of us may have had a camouflage jacket, but mostly we wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of Muslim village guards in that area?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was Mehmed Ahmic, also known as Suduka. Whether he had a lower level commander, I don't know. I know that he was in charge of the political activities and he was the overall commander over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about the first conflict in Ahmici on the 20th of October, 1992? Could you tell us where you were at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I was in my shop and I heard the shooting, and I went out. I heard from my guests that a conflict had broken out between the Muslims and the Croats in the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that early in the morning, the gunfire?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was sometime in the morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear? Why did the conflict break out?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I learnt, subsequently, that the conflict had broken out because Busovaca units were heading for Jajce to assist the defenders of Jajce, and the Muslim guards would not let them pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which were those units from Kiseljak and Busovaca? Were they HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, probably HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of any of the Croats from your village or Ahmici having participated in the conflict over the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you hear, that no Croats took part?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because there was a conflict between the Busovaca units heading for Jajce and the Muslim units in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that conflict did the local people, the local inhabitants of Ahmici take part, the inhabitants of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because they kept guard duty at that roadblock as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you hear the roadblock had been placed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Near the Croatian cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know anything about any trenches having been dug there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, there was one trench in the Croatian cemetery itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that later on?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, because we went to attend mass regularly every Sunday there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about whether any buildings were damaged, any houses on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in my neighbourhood no houses were destroyed, but when I was going to mass at the cemetery I saw that the house of Mehmed Ahmic, also known as Suduka, had been damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about any other houses having been damaged?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about any casualties, anyone killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I heard later that the first victim of that first conflict had been a young man from Kiseljak, and that a man called Pezer, whom I didn't know, had been killed on the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the man from Kiseljak, did you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think his surname was Vidovic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that conflict, do you know that the Muslims left Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had left the area where the village of Ahmici is, but none of our neighbours left in the area of Santici or Zume. None of the Muslims left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So none of the Muslims from Zume left?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the ones who left Ahmici? Did they come back?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of them started returning the very next day, but almost all of them came back within two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that their neighbours, their fellow villagers, their Croats, asked them to come back?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your personal knowledge, did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that we gathered together people to invite them to come back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about some of these houses having been broken into or looted or something stolen?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So nothing was missing from those houses?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I never heard that anything was missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about what happened in Busovaca in January, in early 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that there had been a conflict, but I didn't have any information about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your status in 1993? Were you still participating in the village guards?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did my job until the beginning of war, but every third night I participated in the village guard duty, so I took part every three nights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the others, how many were there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There would be about ten of us in each group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the HVO defence lines against the Serbs in the area?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I know that units went to the defence line in Jajce and also below Vlasic to stop the Serbs from penetrating to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any defence lines against the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was going on or what happened on the 15th of April, 1993, that was the day before the second conflict, did anything special happen or was everything as usual?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing, except that I learned through the media that in Zenica the Muslim units had captured the HVO commander, Zivko Totic, and that they had killed three or four of his escorts, I can't say exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing that day?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As usual, I was working in my restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on the 16th of April in 1993? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That night I slept and in the morning at about half past 5.00, I can't be very precise, I heard gunfire and noise in the street outside. I looked out of the window and I saw people fleeing down the road near my house, so I went out to ask what was going on, and they said that Muslim units had attacked our village and that they were fleeing to a shelter. I went back inside, I took my two young children and my wife, and I went to the shelter with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the gunfire very intense? Could you tell where it was coming from?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was coming from the direction of Busovaca and Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go with your wife and children, to which shelter?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I started toward the house of Jozo Lovric where all the others had been going because this had been our shelter before. When the Serbian planes flew over, we always took shelter there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you meet there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the first person I saw was (redacted) (redacted). He was standing in front of his house on the stairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave the shelter after leaving your wife and children there or did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I stayed for about ten minutes, then I went out to see what was going on, and I met other people coming to the shelter. I talked to them about what was going on, because we didn't know what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet anyone who told you to go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I met Nenad Santic, the commander of my village guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Nenad Santic say to you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nenad told me that I had to go and defend the bridge, Radakov Most, immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did he send you to Radakov Most?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because the main road, the Busovaca-Vitez road near the village of Buhine Kuce had been cut off by the Muslims and we couldn't pass there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the significance of Radakov Most at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was our only route towards Vitez, and the only road from Busovaca to Vitez. Yes, it was a country road, and the only one we could use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far from your house, approximately, was Radakov Most?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I can't be precise, but 300 to 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far Buhine Kuce is from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Buhine Kuce is about 800 to 1.000 kilometres -- metres, sorry, metres away from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the village of Buhine Kuce near the main road?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Nenad Santic sent you to Radakov Most. Do you remember what else he said?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He said that I would find Drago Vidovic there and Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he said that they would join you in the guard?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you already been in the area, or were you already in the area of Radakov Most when Dragan Papic came?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there, I found Drago Vidovic there, and some ten minutes later we saw Dragan Papic coming from the Busovaca side, from the village of Rovna crossing the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was it, approximately? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was at about half past six, between half past six and seven, I can't be precise as to the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is it time for a break, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Actually, we have five more minutes. Would you like a break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: No, we can go on. I thought it was time for a break. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Puliselic, before we go on, could you have the bridge pointed out, please, so we can understand what the witness is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I intended to do that in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, would you show where the bridge, Radakov Most, is?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my house here. This is the road leading from the main road toward the bridge, and the bridge is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does the road go toward Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here. Here. You can see a little bit of it (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The road goes on where?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the village of Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can sit down now. You said that Dragan Papic arrived from the direction of Donja Rovna over the bridge?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say? What had he been doing there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He said that he was a little late because he had taken his mother, wife and sister to the shelter in Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His mother, his wife and his sister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Donja Rovna on the other side of the bridge were there any guards? Did you see any guards?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say who you saw there? Did you recognise the people?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There were several. I knew two of them. One was Zvonko Santic and the other was Jozo Alilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps we might have a break now, because we have some aerial photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. A 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, let us go back to this aerial photograph. You said -- you showed us where your house was. You said that the area was called Zume. You showed us where the bridge, Radakov Most, is. Can you now show us where Ahmici is, where Pirici is, where Santici is, the direction of the road from Busovaca, the location of the Catholic cemetery, and so on.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the main road, the Busovaca/Vitez main road. This is the Croatian cemetery, and the village of Ahmici begins here and stretches in this direction. And this is the road that leads to the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the village of Ahmici stretch to below the road?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is part here with quite a lot of Muslims who lived here, and there were more houses -- a few houses below the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the village of Santici?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here (indicating). Santici is here. This road passes by my house. And this road leads to the village of Pirici, while this other one leads to the village of Santici. And this area here is the village of Santici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the village of Santici is mostly only on one side of the road, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your hamlet of Zume --

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is Zume. This circle here. There is a sports centre here, a stadium, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we could say that Zume is between Pirici and Ahmici; could we say that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, between Pirici and Ahmici is where Zume is. So from here, up there is Ahmici, and Zume is down below.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you show us Donja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Donja Rovna stretches here. Before the turning for Santici, there is another turning, you cross the bridge, Radakov bridge, and it's here, in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we say that Donja Rovna was on the right bank of the River Lasva?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, downstream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this also in another municipality?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's in the Busovaca municipality. The Busovaca and Vitez municipalities are separated by the River Lasva. Vitez is on the right and Busovaca is on the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Vidovic, you may sit down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D4/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, this is the same aerial photograph you have been showing, but on a smaller scale?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to show us on this photograph your house and to put a circle around it with a felt pen.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there's one here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a red marker and put the circle around your house on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark it with the letter "V." I would now like to ask you to put a circle round the bridge, Radakov Most. Could you put the letter "B" here, where the bridge is.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you put a line showing where you were on guard with Dragan Vidovic and Dragan Papovic. Could you mark it "1."

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the other side of the bridge, could you mark the area where the guards were on that side. Could you mark this "2." Now I would like to ask you on this aerial photograph the road leading from Busovaca, and to mark it as far as the turning towards the bridge, Radakov Most. So would you mark the road. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the newly established route?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean towards Vitez?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, up to the bridge. And then as far as we can see in the direction of Vitez. This turning, it wasn't an asphalt road leading to the village along the river?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was a macadam road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the first village along that road?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where do this road go on? Does it cross the River Lasva again?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, it crosses another river, a smaller river, Rnska (phoen).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where does it come again?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after the village of Rijeka, it comes out on the Vitez-Busovaca main road again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this junction, how far is it from Vitez, approximately?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe one kilometre from the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: The usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D5/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, what does this photograph show? You can look at it on your monitor, if you like.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It shows the bridge, Radakov Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does this road lead from?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It leads from the village of Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to the nearer road. Where does it lead from? The village of Rovna would be on the other side of the bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This road comes from the direction of my house, from the main road. So it leads -- yes, it leads by Ljubosove Kuce across the bridge to Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the houses we can see on the other side of the bridge is Donja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, those are Radakove Kuce in Donja Rovna, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you put an arrow on the photograph showing the direction from which you came to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you put a cross on the bridge itself, to mark the bridge.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may sit down now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D6/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know whether the first document has been entered under the correct number. What was the number? Was it 4, or 40?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, what does this photograph show? What is this?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Radakov Most, the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What side has this been taken from? Is it taken from the side where you were on guard? It's not a very good photograph.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were keeping guard here, in this area, on our side where we were keeping guard. And this is Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were keeping watch; and were you standing on one spot, or were you moving?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't move across the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I didn't mean across the bridge; I mean --

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we walked up and down for about 50 metres along the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may sit down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D7/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, what does this photograph show?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It shows the bridge, Radakov Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which position? From which spot?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, downstream, on the Busovaca side. From the Busovaca side, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: We have two more photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D8/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, what does this photograph show, and where was it taken from?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It shows the bridge, Radakov Most, from the Busovaca side. It was taken from the Busovaca side, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The houses that can be seen on the other side of the bridge, they're called Ljubosove Kuce. Pero Ljubas's houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you on guard continually, or did you take a break? Did you have a rest?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since we had only two weapons, two of us always kept watch while one rested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put a circle or an "X" where you rested? Put a small circle there.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that from time to time, when it was possible, you moved from the bridge for some 20 or 30 metres upstream and downstream?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw a line on the other side of the bridge showing approximately -- to show us where you moved. Where did you see the other guards on the other side of the bridge? Where were they, roughly?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they also move?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, only on the other side of the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the guards on the other side used any trenches? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: One more photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D9/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, what can be seen on this photograph, and where was it taken from?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is the Radak bridge, taken from Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again we see those same houses?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Ljubas houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please mark once again with a circle where the guards rested.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. On that day, the 16th of April, 1993, did you keep watch duty throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to move away from those positions assigned to you for that day, the next day, and the days that followed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We had strict orders not to move away from the Radak bridge. We were not allowed to move away from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned weapons: How were you armed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We had two M-48 rifles, known as Tandzaras.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are military weapons?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are rifles with single shots, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how you were dressed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We were dressed, me and Drago Vidovic, in civilian clothes. Dragan Papic had a camouflage jacket and jeans on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had a camouflage jacket. Can you tell us whether there were any insignia on that jacket?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this spot where you were keeping guard duty and that you have indicated on the photograph, is it possible to see Ahmici from there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, because it is in the valley of the Lasva River. All you can see is Donja Rovna at the river and a couple of houses there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything special on Dragan Papic's face?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean on his face?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise Dragan Papic here in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see anything on his face now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but at the time he had a long beard. He had a long beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he had a much longer beard than he has now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His beard was up to here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, Counsel Puliselic. The interpreters are asking whether you could speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Dragan told you that he had taken his mother, sister and wife to Donja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that his wife was in advanced pregnancy?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When he came to join us he said that he had taken his wife, mother and sister away because she was expecting, and she was expecting delivery any day soon and that's why he felt he needed to move her away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, could we show a videotape?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: May I observe that this videotape that we're going to see, that it was filmed on the 21st of October, 1998, showing a part of the road -- a part of Vitez and the road from Vitez along Buhine Kuce, Ahmici and the Catholic cemetery, and then we come back through Ahmici and turn off towards Radak's bridge. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, I'm now going to ask you to occasionally comment on this videotape. Can you please tell us where we are now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the road coming from Rijeka and joining the main road, and it leads across Radak's bridge. Yes, this is the road to Radak's bridge viewed from the direction of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where we saw the car go?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The car has gone towards Radak's bridge via the village of Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we fast forward the tape briefly? Slowly please, slowly, slowly. Where are we heading for now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We're heading towards the former railway station in Vitez, the plant called Impregnacija. So this is the junction, separate where the road forks off from the main Busovaca-Travnik road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop, please. Stop, stop, stop, stop. Will you wind the tape back a little? Stop. Stop. Slightly more forward. Can you see the signpost?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Their Honours can't see clearly. Stop there, please. So the signpost points towards Travnik, to the left.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a transit road, and to the right leading to Sarajevo. If you take the road to Sarajevo you reach Busovaca passing through Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us proceed with the tape, please. You can fast wind now. That's it. That's enough. Slowly, please. Is Buhine Kuce anywhere near there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we're just approaching there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you stop? A little further forward. Forward, please. A little more. You can see them, yes. It's fine. Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These are Ljubas's houses on the left, left and right of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go on, please, with the tape. So the road was cut here somewhere?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Right here. Right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the road leading now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's leading to Busovaca, or, rather, the village of Zume and Santici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can fast wind briefly. Slowly now. Slowly, please. This is the road leading to Radak's bridge, to the right.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is that road leading to Radak's bridge. So when we're coming from the direction of Vitez, then you turn right to Radak's bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we mentioned another road, the Rijeka street leading to Radak's bridge.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this is the second road leading towards the Lasva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are we now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We're close to my house now. This is the road leading to Radak's bridge down there. The camera is just turning around. Yes, this is the road branching off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we can forward wind, quickly, please. Stop. Stop, please. Will you wind back the tape briefly? Mr. Vidovic, whose house is this?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is Dragan Papic's house and the house of his parents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who owns that house?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ivo Papic is the owner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's it. Stop there, please. Do you know who lived in that house?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean before the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Before the war who lived there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan's parents, Dragan, his wife, his sister and his brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let us proceed. There are a lot of cars there both in front and behind the house, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fast forward, please. Stop. Stop, just for a minute, please. There we see -- will you wind the tape back a little so that we can see the whole house? We can see some damage on the house, can't we? There are some holes on the walls. You don't know what caused those holes?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This happened on the 16th of April, when the conflict occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can go on then. We can fast forward now. Stop. Stop, please. Where are we now? What can be seen to the left?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the Croatian cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the Catholic cemetery?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we have a view of the cemetery from the direction of Busovaca. So really we should go back now. Will you play the tape, please? Can you fast wind, please? Stop, please. We can go on, fast wind, fast wind. Stop there, please. Where does this road lead?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is leading to Radak's bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from the main road going from the direction of Busovaca, we have turned off the main road and we're going along the road that you marked on the photograph, towards Radak's bridge. We're going downhill now. Whose house is this?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the -- the man is called Grebenar. I don't know his first name. Maybe Nikica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these are mostly Croatian houses?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we see Radak's bridge, I think.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is Ljubas's houses, and over there is Radak's bridge and behind is Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is where you kept guard duty?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can go on with the tape. So we're crossing Radak's bridge?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this, to the left is Donja Rovna and to the right Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the road along which we came, leading to the main road Busovaca-Vitez, and this is Ljubas's houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is where you rested?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where that garage door is?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, not here, over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here. This is where you rested?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. We can go on now. Fast wind forward, please. Stop. So this is a shot from where?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now -- where are we going now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We're going towards the village of Rijeka, towards Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upstream parallel with the Lasva River?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the macadam road, the only one we could use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Radak's bridge to Rijeka village, how far is it, how many kilometres?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It may be two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. We can fast wind forward, please. Towards Rijeka. Stop. Are we close to Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is a small stream here called Vranjska, just before the village of Rijeka. There's a small bridge across it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have we reached the village of Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, once we cross the bridge. And to the left again is the Busovaca municipality and this is where we crossed the bridge. So we're now moving from one municipality to another. The bridge is the boarder. So we're now on the left bank of the Lasva River?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, this is not Lasva. This is Vranjska. This is the river of Vranjska. We're far from the Lasva River now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is the village of Rijeka. We can fast forward now, please. Stop. Where are we now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is still the village of Rijeka. There's quite a bit until you reach the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fast wind, please. Stop.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So we're approaching the main road now, which, to the right, leads to Busovaca and, to the left, to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we're now in the road that we saw at the beginning called Rijecka Ulica.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here we are reaching the main road now. To the right it leads to Busovaca, to the left to Vitez. Down there are Buhine Kuce, to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we're now going towards Vitez. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the videotape is numbered D10/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, can you answer the following question: For how many days -- for how long was Dragan Papic on guard duty with you at Radak's bridge?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not for long. Maybe eight to ten days. I would not be able to tell you with greater precision. And then he left. He told us that his wife had had a baby, and he left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he left when his wife had delivered the baby?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether Dragan Papic, at any point in time during that period of eight to ten days, moved away from your guard duty area except for resting in that house that you pointed out?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, because we were not allowed to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you quite certain that he didn't move away on the 16th and 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm quite certain. Throughout that period none of us were allowed to move from that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he left when he heard that his wife had had the baby?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about where he went after that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. I heard later, maybe 15 or 20 days later, that he had been assigned to the frontline, but I don't know where or how. I didn't see him after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us for how long you remained on guard duty?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until the 24th of August there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for more than five months?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave then?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I fell seriously ill and I had to go for treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Dragan Papic was employed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Papic was employed in the forestry administration as a forester.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HVO at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I know, because Dragan worked as a forester until the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So until the conflict of the 16th of April, '93, he was employed in the forestry administration, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about Dragan Papic and his family? You said that his wife had delivered. What did he get? Was it a son or a daughter?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't learn anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know today, the children that he has?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know even today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the conflict would he visit your catering establishment?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any guests there usually?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were. There were both Muslims and Croats who gathered there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time hear Dragan Papic talking about politics, discussing political topics, expressing a negative attitude towards Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard that? What did he usually talk about?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I could understand, he liked to discuss girls, he liked to talk about the cars he was fixing, about anecdotes with regard to his forestry work and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he repair cars? Was it a hobby of his?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I often saw him and there were usually several cars in front of his house, but I personally never had my car repaired there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but did you know that he fixed his friends' cars?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and he always talked about it. He always talked about how -- what a good mechanic he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Muslims go to him?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or did you ever see that he used to go to the mosque when a Muslim who had died was being honoured?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we all attended funerals, the Muslims attended our funerals and we attended theirs. If anyone died, we always went to each other's funerals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him and his father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him occasionally wear some kind of uniform before the conflict with the Muslims, and since when?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I often saw him wearing his forester's uniform, and before the conflict he wore the forestry uniform and the camouflage jacket with it. I can't remember exactly what it was like, but it was some kind of camouflage jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that occasionally he wore a uniform since the outbreak of the conflict with the Serbs? Did you see him wear any uniform considerably before these events?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I always saw him with a camouflage jacket and jeans, so it was a combination, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you knew his father, Ivo?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know him well?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Ivo Papic's occupation?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was the only plumber in the area for these two villages, for Zume, Santici, Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he had a lot of work?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he do any plumbing in Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Water was brought in from Krusica and he did the plumbing for everyone. There were no other plumbers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he is still doing plumbing for the Muslims returning to Ahmici in the area?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard about this?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes see a flag on his house, and what kind of flag was it?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the chequerboard flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it there all the time or only occasionally, and if it was there occasionally, when?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only on religious holidays, and then it wasn't only on his house but my house too, because we all had flags when it was a religious holiday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Muslims also display their own flags on their houses, on their holidays?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mehmed Ahmic? You mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his nickname?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Suduka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Mehmed Ahmic's occupation?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to start with, he had a catering establishment like me, until the elections. Then he took over the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member, was he in the leadership of the party?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was in the leadership. I think he was the chief person in the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that area?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the Ahmici area. I don't know about Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did his attitude towards the Croats change? Do you know anything about his attitude toward the Croats after the multi-party elections?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after the elections everybody changed. People were not the same as they had been before. Everyone had their own ethnic affiliation, and so did he.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Abdulah Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Fahrudin Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that there were two Fahrudin Ahmics?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. I knew only one. He was a musician. He played seven days before the conflict broke out, he and Kupreskic played in my establishment together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was in your establishment?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were having a celebration celebrating Easter. It was Easter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Fahrudin Ahmic's house, in what part of the village?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: His house was on the Vitez-Busovaca main road about 100 metres away from my house, in the direction of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1993, you were probably not aware, apart from the fact that you heard gunfire, you probably didn't know what was happening in Ahmici. Did you learn later what had happened there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as soon as I arrived in the shelter, I was told by the women who had fled from Ahmici, the Croatian women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They said that Muslim units had attacked the Croats, so they had fled, and that they had fled to our area, because there were more Croats there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That was what the women said. But what did you learn later? Were there many people killed later? What happened to their houses?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, many people were killed on both sides. That was the information I heard, that Mirjan Santic was the first victim of the clash, that he had been on the -- on the Croatian side and guard, and that he had been killed by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were a lot of Muslims killed. Do you remember, because you mentioned Mirjan -- what did you say -- Santic, do you remember any other Croats who were killed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A lot of people were killed, Ivica Vidovic, Zlatan Ivankovic. A lot of Croats. I can't remember all their names, but if I saw a list I might remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there Muslims returning to Ahmici now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Almost all of them have returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your relationship with them now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am on good terms with them now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As before?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They come to my catering establishment, have a drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They pass by through our hamlet, regularly, the ones from Pirici and Ahmici, and there has never been an incident since they came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there are no incidents now?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have completed my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we will now break and adjourn until tomorrow morning. But let me just ask Counsel Krajina whether he intends to examine this witness in chief, tomorrow morning I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President, my colleague, Mr. Par, will examine in the morning and it will take 30 to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. We adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
